test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A carburetor used in a petrol engine is designed so as to fit in which of the following parts of the engine?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cylinder head.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• A carburetor is an essential component used in petrol engines to mix air and fuel for combustion.
 
• It is usually fitted on the cylinder head of the engine.
 
• The cylinder head houses the intake and exhaust valves, and the carburetor is attached to facilitate air-fuel mixture delivery.
 
• The carburetor ensures the correct ratio of air and fuel, which is critical for optimal engine performance.
 
• Modern petrol engines may use fuel injection systems instead of carburetors, but carburetors are still found in older and smaller engines.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Connecting Rod:**

 
 
• The connecting rod connects the piston to the crankshaft in an engine.
 
• It transmits the force exerted by the combustion process to the crankshaft.
 
 
 
• **Casing:**
 
 
• The casing typically refers to the outer covering or housing of a component.
 
• It is not directly related to the carburetor's functioning.
 
 
 
• **Piston:**
 
 
• The piston is a cylindrical component that moves up and down within the cylinder.
 
• It plays a key role in the combustion process by compressing the air-fuel mixture.
